title: platform/analytics.json
description: The analytics providers a dealer has enabled, baked by the platform on every publish. Platform-owned and regenerated wholesale — an edit here is lost on the next publish, and until it is lost this dealer is tagged in a way nobody else is. A dealer in no programme has no such file at all, and their built site then contains no third-party code and no third-party URL.

runtimeVersion.description: The renderer version this repo is on, for providers that report a site technology version.

providers.description: Only enabled providers appear. An empty array is meaningful: it is a dealer who turned every provider off, and the head emits nothing.

vocabularies.description: Closed vocabularies site/ must author against, keyed by name — today just pageTypes. The intersection of the enabled providers' lists, because a page carries one pageType and every provider that names it receives that same value. It is the same map the dashboard builds its select from, so a value a dealer was offered cannot be one their build then refuses. Absent or empty leaves the field unconstrained.

id.description: The descriptor id the platform registered this provider under.

adapterUrl.description: Absolute URL of the adapter that maps platform event names onto this vendor's calls. Loaded async by the runtime, because everything with a deadline is already done by the head bootstrap.

settings.description: This dealer's values for the provider. PUBLIC: they are baked into a static file on the dealer's own domain and served over the Shop API. An API key must never be stored here.

consentCategory.description: The consent category this provider falls under, when the dealer's consent tool distinguishes them.

requiredForProduction.description: Settings keys whose value must not be a REPLACE_ placeholder. Copied from the descriptor so scripts/build.mjs can refuse a production build without knowing what the provider is.

bootstrap.description: The synchronous head tag. Present when the vendor requires its own tag in the head; absent when the adapter alone is enough. Nothing here is evaluated as code: the renderer interpolates these values into a fixed queueing-stub shape through JSON.stringify.

globalName.description: The global the vendor's script expects. A bare identifier, because it is written into executable code.

globalKind.description: Whether the global is a function that queues its arguments (the sd/ga shape) or a plain array the vendor's script drains (the dataLayer shape). Emitting the wrong one breaks the tag outright — a queue vendor calls .push and a function has none — so it is declared rather than guessed. Defaults to function.

script.description: The vendor script, loaded async after the stub and its calls.

calls.description: Calls made on the stub before the page call, each an argument list.

pageCall.description: Leading arguments of the page call. The page facts and this dealer's settings are appended as one object.

readyCall.description: The call that sends the first page view. Its presence is what tells the runtime not to send that page view again.

pageKeys.description: Platform page-fact name -> this vendor's name for it. A fact with no entry is not sent, which is how a provider opts out of one without the renderer knowing the fact exists.

pageValues.description: Platform page-fact name -> a map from the platform's own words to this vendor's. The storefront derives a page's kind from its route and knows no provider, so it emits a platform kind and this translates it. A value with no entry passes through untouched, which is what lets a brand-site page authored in the vendor's own vocabulary work through the same path.
